alerts.title: Abdominal pain may signal TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort and decreased appetite as presenting signs of TDF toxicity including lactic acidosis, Fanconi syndrome, and acute kidney injury, warranting LFTs and RFTs when these symptoms occur. Patient is on TDF and reports abdominal pain today. Appetite is preserved and no fever is noted, which makes infection less likely but does not exclude drug toxicity. No LFTs or repeat RFTs have been ordered in the clinician's plan. Serum creatinine 78 days ago was normal at 82 umol/L, arguing against established nephrotoxicity, but no renal or hepatic assessment has been done since the symptom began.

evidence.recommended_action: Order LFTs and serum creatinine/eGFR to evaluate for TDF toxicity. If deranged, consider substituting TDF per guideline algorithm.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia at 25 copies/mL
alerts.message: Guidelines note that viral load above suppression threshold is associated with risk of transmission and subsequent virologic non-suppression, and WHO guidance addresses monitoring of low-level viremia. Patient's latest viral load is 25 copies/mL (2025-11-05), which is detectable though below the 200 copies/mL plasma suppression cutoff. This is not treatment failure but indicates low-level viremia that warrants enhanced monitoring. No repeat viral load or adherence assessment appears in the clinician's plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess adherence and repeat viral load at next scheduled visit per routine monitoring algorithm to confirm suppression.
